content: 1. Digoxin levels are increased by the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 2. Moexipril raises digoxin levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor. 3. Moxifloxacin increases digoxin levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 4. Nabumetone and digoxin both elevate serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor. 5. Nadolol and digoxin both increase serum potassium levels. Nadolol enhances digoxin effects via pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to enhanced bradycardia. Use caution and monitor. 6. Nafcillin increases digoxin levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 7. Naproxen and digoxin both elevate serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor. 8. Nebivolol and digoxin both increase serum potassium levels. Nebivolol enhances digoxin effects via pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to enhanced bradycardia. Use caution and monitor. 9. Nefazodone increases digoxin levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 10. Oral neomycin increases digoxin levels or effects by altering intestinal flora but decreases digoxin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 11. Neratinib increases digoxin levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Neratinib inhibits P-gp transport. Exercise caution when coadministered with a P-gp substrate with a narrow therapeutic index. Use caution and monitor. 12. Nicardipine increases digoxin levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 13. Nifedipine increases digoxin levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and may reduce digoxin clearance, leading to increased plasma concentrations and toxicity risk. Adjust the digoxin dose as needed. Use caution and monitor. 14. Nilotinib increases digoxin levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 15. Nirmatrelvir increases digoxin levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Measure serum digoxin concentrations before initiating nirmatrelvir/ritonavir. Reduce the digoxin dose by approximately 30-50% or modify dosing frequency, and continue monitoring during coadministration. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Nitrofurantoin increases digoxin levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 17. Digoxin increases serum potassium, while norepinephrine decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear. Use caution and monitor. 18. Ofloxacin increases digoxin levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Digoxin increases ofloxacin levels or effects by competing for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor. 19. Olmesartan and digoxin both elevate serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor. 20. Omeprazole increases digoxin toxicity through prolonged use of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), which may cause hypomagnesemia and increase the risk of digoxin toxicity. Use caution and monitor. 21. Oxaprozin and digoxin both elevate serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor. 22. Topical oxymetazoline decreases digoxin effects via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor. 23. Digoxin reduces catecholamine reuptake at nerve terminals, making blood vessels more sensitive to endogenous or exogenous catecholamines. 24. Oxytetracycline increases digoxin levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 25. Hypercalcemia induced by parathyroid hormone or paloparathyroid hormone analogs may predispose patients to digitalis toxicity. Monitor for signs and symptoms of digoxin toxicity if coadministered. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 26. Pantoprazole increases digoxin toxicity through prolonged PPI use, which may cause hypomagnesemia and increase the risk of digoxin toxicity. Use caution and monitor. 27. Parecoxib and digoxin both elevate serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor. 28. Paricalcitol increases digoxin toxicity via pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor. 29. Paromomycin increases digoxin levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 30. Penbutolol and digoxin both elevate serum potassium levels. Penbutolol enhances digoxin effects via pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to enhanced bradycardia. Use caution and monitor. 31. Perindopril increases digoxin levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor. 32. Phenobarbital decreases digoxin levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 33. Phenytoin decreases digoxin levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 34. Pindolol and digoxin both elevate serum potassium levels. Pindolol enhances digoxin effects via pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to enhanced bradycardia. Use caution and monitor. 35. Digoxin increases serum potassium, while pirbuterol decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear. Use caution and monitor. 36. Piroxicam and digoxin both elevate serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor. 37. Pirtobrutinib increases digoxin levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Pirtobrutinib, a P-gp inhibitor, may increase plasma concentrations of sensitive P-gp substrates, raising the risk of adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor. 38. Ponatinib increases digoxin levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 39. Posaconazole increases digoxin levels by decreasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 40. Potassium acid phosphate and digoxin both elevate serum potassium levels. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 41. Potassium chloride and digoxin both elevate serum potassium levels. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 42. Digoxin increases pramipexole levels or effects by competing for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor. 43. Pretomanid increases digoxin levels or effects. Increased monitoring for drug-related adverse effects is recommended if pretomanid is coadministered with sensitive OATP1B3 or P-gp substrates. Use caution and monitor. 44. Procarbazine decreases digoxin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 45. Propantheline increases digoxin levels or effects through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Measure serum digoxin concentrations before initiating concomitant drugs. Reduce the digoxin dose by approximately 15-30% or modify dosing frequency, and continue monitoring. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Propranolol and digoxin both elevate serum potassium levels. Propranolol enhances digoxin effects via pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to enhanced bradycardia. Use caution and monitor. 47. Quercetin decreases digoxin levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 48. Quinapril increases digoxin levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor. 49. Digoxin increases quinine levels or effects by competing for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor. 50. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases digoxin levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 51. Rabeprazole increases digoxin toxicity through prolonged PPI use, which may cause hypomagnesemia and increase the risk of digoxin toxicity. Use caution and monitor. 52. Ramipril increases digoxin levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor. 53. Ranolazine increases digoxin levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and by decreasing metabolism. Ranolazine inhibits P-glycoprotein. Use caution and monitor. 54. Regorafenib decreases digoxin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Chemotherapy may reduce digoxin absorption; monitor levels and adjust digoxin dose accordingly. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 55. Rifabutin decreases digoxin levels by increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 56. Rifampin decreases digoxin levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and by increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 57. Rifapentine decreases digoxin levels by increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 58. Ritonavir increases digoxin levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter by decreasing renal and hepatic clearance. Plasma concentrations and pharmacologic effects of digoxin may be increased. Use caution and monitor. 59. Rolapitant increases digoxin levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Oral rolapitant, a P-gp inhibitor, may increase plasma concentrations of P-gp substrates, potentially leading to adverse reactions. Monitor digoxin concentrations with concomitant rolapitant use and adjust dosage if necessary. Use caution and monitor. 60. Sacubitril/valsartan and digoxin both elevate serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor. 61. Non-ASA salicylates and digoxin both elevate serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor. 62. Digoxin increases serum potassium, while salmeterol decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear. Use caution and monitor. 63. Salsalate and digoxin both elevate serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor. 64. Sarecycline increases digoxin levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor for toxicities of P-gp substrates that may require dosage reduction when coadministered with P-gp inhibitors. Use caution and monitor. 65. Senna increases digoxin toxicity due to potassium depletion. Use caution and monitor. 66. Sevelamer decreases digoxin levels by increasing elimination. Use caution and monitor. 67. Simvastatin increases digoxin levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 68. Sirolimus increases digoxin levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 69. Sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid decreases digoxin levels by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer digoxin at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose to avoid chelation with magnesium. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 70. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride decreases digoxin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Administer digoxin at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose to avoid chelation with magnesium. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 71. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate decreases digoxin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Administer digoxin at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose to avoid chelation with magnesium. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 72. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases digoxin levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Velpatasvir inhibits P-gp. Monitor digoxin levels if coadministered. Refer to digoxin prescribing information for monitoring and dose modification recommendations for digoxin concentration increases of <50%. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 73. Sotagliflozin increases digoxin levels or effects through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Increased exposure to digoxin occurs when coadministered with sotagliflozin 400 mg. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 74. Sotalol and digoxin both elevate serum potassium levels. Sotalol enhances digoxin effects via pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to enhanced bradycardia. Use caution and monitor. 75. Spironolactone and digoxin both elevate serum potassium levels. Spironolactone increases digoxin levels by decreasing renal clearance and may cause false elevation of digoxin assay. Use caution and monitor. 76. St. John’s Wort decreases digoxin levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and by increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 77. Stiripentol increases digoxin levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Consider reducing the dose of P-gp substrates if adverse reactions occur when coadministered with stiripentol. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 78. Streptomycin increases digoxin levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 79. Digoxin and succinylcholine both elevate serum potassium levels. The mechanism is unknown. Increased risk of cardiac arrhythmias. Use caution and monitor. 80. Sulfadiazine increases digoxin levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 81. Sulfamethoxazole increases digoxin levels or effects by altering intestinal flora and by competing for renal tubular clearance. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 82. Sulfasalazine and digoxin both elevate serum potassium levels. Sulfasalazine decreases digoxin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. Sulfasalazine doses >2 g/day may exacerbate this effect. 83. Sulfisoxazole increases digoxin levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 84. Sulindac and digoxin both elevate serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor. 85. Suvorexant increases digoxin levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Suvorexant may cause a slight increase in digoxin levels. Use caution and monitor. 86. Tacrolimus increases digoxin levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 87. Teduglutide increases digoxin levels by enhancing absorption of concomitant oral medications. Exercise caution with drugs requiring titration or those with a narrow therapeutic index. Use caution and monitor.
